title: 2013-01 — Dunn and Pesnell vs. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained. The SJC answered the stated issue “No” and held that the Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery’s November 17, 2012 adoption of its Complaint Commission’s recommendation to institute process and proceed to trial stands. The SJC noted that the adopted recommendation may still be subject to subsequent parliamentary procedure for final disposition. It did not decide TE David Swavely’s guilt.
first_summary: The SJC heard an appeal from two teaching elders challenging Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery’s decision to institute process and try TE David Swavely. The SJC denied the appeal, holding that any procedural errors did not require reversal and that the presbytery’s recommendation to proceed to trial stands.
summary: The complaint challenged Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery’s November 17, 2012 vote adopting its Complaint Commission’s recommendation to institute process and try TE David Swavely. The SJC did not sustain it. Although the record showed possible procedural irregularities—including unauthorized circulation of an earlier complaint—the SJC found no reversible error: presbyteries receive deference on factual records and broad latitude to judge the sufficiency of investigations. The recommendation to proceed to trial stands, subject to later parliamentary action. The SJC did not decide Swavely’s guilt.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2013-01, Dunn and Pesnell vs. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery, SJC, 42nd GA (2014). Opinion jointly by TE Paul Kooistra and TE Will Barker, adopted by the Panel, amended by the SJC (lines 133–134), and adopted by vote of 18 concurring, 2 abstaining, 1 not qualified, 3 absent (lines 136–142).
evidence_notes.dispute: The issue was whether Presbytery erred on November 17, 2012, when it adopted the Complaint Commission’s recommendation—first made in November 2011—to institute process and proceed toward trial (line 49). The complaint was re-filed by TE Dwight Dunn and TE Darin Pesnell (line 41).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered “No,” leaving the adopted recommendation to institute process and proceed to trial standing, with a note that later parliamentary procedure could still affect final disposition (line 53). Reasoning found no reversible error, deferring to the presbytery on the record and investigation, and addressing Matthew 18/BCO 31-5, BCO 32-20 limitations, circularization/BCO 43-2, BCO 43-8/43-9, and BCO 32-19 attorney involvement (lines 57–132).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC did not determine TE Swavely’s guilt; it upheld only the authority to proceed to trial. The table records concurrences, abstentions, a not-qualified vote, and absences, but no separate dissent (lines 136–142). The text’s reference at line 45 to the Panel hearing the “Appeal” is not the operative procedural label; the issue and judgment decide a complaint against Presbytery’s action.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The prior SJC Case 2012-04 is referenced as procedural history: the complaint was administratively out of order because the December 2011 complaint had not been referred to the FCC by a vote of Presbytery and the FCC’s conclusion had not been voted on by Presbytery (line 37). No full prior decision is incorporated by reference in the supplied source, and its supplied result is treated only as history.

source_limits: The supplied source is the SJC opinion and vote. It does not include the full Record of the Case, Presbytery minutes, the Complaint Commission’s complete report, or the prior Case 2012-04 decision. Factual details and quotations are drawn from the SJC’s summary and reasoning, not independently verified from underlying records.

C20 — an unexplained disposition must remain unexplained; contrast this reasoned decision, which states its no-reversible-error rationale.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged Presbytery action: its November 17, 2012 adoption of the Complaint Commission recommendation to institute process and proceed to trial.
score_reasons.decision: States the single material outcome: complaint not sustained, recommendation stands, with the parliamentary-procedure qualification.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the adopted no-reversible-error rationale, including deference to Presbytery and latitude on investigation sufficiency.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the useful limits: circularization did not require reversal where fair trial was not jeopardized, “biblical mediation” was constitutionally nebulous, and guilt was not decided.
score_reasons.fidelity: Distinguishes complaint from appeal, historical FCC and PMWP actions from the SJC’s adopted judgment, and does not convert allegations into findings of guilt.
